scores.question: Did Nvidia beat its revenue guidance for fiscal Q2 2027?
scores.answer:
Yes. Nvidia guided fiscal Q2 2027 revenue to $91.0 billion, plus or minus 2%, excluding any Data Center compute revenue from China [1]. It reported revenue of $96,221M (about $96.2 billion) in its 10-Q for that quarter [2]. That is above the top of the range, $5.2 billion or 5.7% above the $91.0 billion point estimate [1].

scores.question: What is the trend in Meta's capex over the last four quarters, Q3 2025 to Q2 2026?
scores.answer:
Meta's quarterly capex rose overall from Q3 2025 to Q2 2026, with one dip in Q1 2026. Quarterly capex was $18,829M in Q3 2025 [1], $21,383M in Q4 2025 [2], $18,997M in Q1 2026 [3] and $30,116M in Q2 2026 [4].
- Q3 to Q4 2025: up 13.56% [1][2].
- Q4 2025 to Q1 2026: down 11.16% [2][3].
- Q1 to Q2 2026: up 58.53% [3][4].
- Overall, Q3 2025 to Q2 2026: up 59.94% [1][4].
The highest quarter, Q2 2026 at $30,116M, exceeded the lowest, Q3 2025 at $18,829M, by $11,287M [1][4].
The Q2 2026 figure is derived as six-month year-to-date capex less Q1 2026 [4], and the Q3 2025 and Q4 2025 figures are also derived from year-to-date totals [1][2].

Sources:
[1] META 10-Q filed 2025-10-30: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1326801/000162828025047240/meta-20250930.htm

scores.question: According to Nvidia's 10-Q MD&A for fiscal Q2 2027, what drove the growth in Data Center revenue?
failure_details: 0 numbers_grounded: '$89,023 million' is in no evidence: Data Center revenue for the quarter was $89,023 million [E4].
scores.answer:
Nvidia's 10-Q MD&A for fiscal Q2 2027 attributes the growth in Data Center revenue to the ramp of Blackwell Ultra infrastructure. Data Center revenue was $89.0 billion, up 117% from a year ago and up 18% sequentially [1].
- Hyperscale: revenue more than doubled from a year ago and rose 13% sequentially, on the strength of Blackwell Ultra [1].
- ACIE: revenue rose 138% year over year and 25% sequentially, driven by end-demand from AI natives, enterprises and sovereign customers, as well as hyperscalers using AI clouds [1].

Sources:
[1] NVDA 10-Q FY2027Q2, Item 2. Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations, characters 84229-86247: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1045810/000104581026000075/nvda-20260726.htm

scores.question: What does Tesla's 10-K say in its risk factors about depending on Elon Musk?
failure_details: 0 llm_unsupported: The language appears in the key employees risk factor and a standalone risk factor in FY2023 and FY2024 10-Ks.: E1/E2 are standalone; E3/E4 key-employee factor; but both appear in both years, so suppo
scores.answer:
Tesla's 10-K risk factors say the company is highly dependent on Elon Musk. A standalone risk factor, headed "We are highly dependent on the services of Elon Musk, Technoking of Tesla and our Chief Executive Officer," appears in the FY2023 and FY2024 10-Ks [1][2]. It says Mr. Musk "does not devote his full time and attention to Tesla" and holds management positions at other companies, including Space Exploration Technologies Corp. [2].
Musk is also named in the key-employee risk factor, which says Tesla is "highly dependent on the services of Elon Musk" and that none of its key employees is bound by an employment agreement for any specific term [3][4].
The FY2025 10-K excerpts I retrieved did not include the Musk dependence language, so I cannot confirm its wording in that filing [5][6]. That filing does include a risk factor on the 2025 CEO Performance Award, but the excerpt does not tie it to Musk dependence [7].

Sources:
[1] TSLA 10-K FY2023Q4, ITEM 1A. RISK FACTORS, characters 89357-91730: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1318605/000162828024002390/tsla-20231231.htm
